label: PF Backlog 601
title: EDP-20: Append-only AuditStore; split orchestrator/storage.py (audit vs cache vs evidence); retention/redaction; large checkpoints -> object store

delivery.note: EDP-20 slice 1: partitioning, swap, retention, holds, coverage; PG16 suite + precheck PASS; Gate 2.5 0 pending.

decisions.note: Gate 1 approved with attention. Gate 1.5: 17 findings actioned, 0 pending. Decisions: canonical audit_id_seq; 14d backup rollback window; 90d purge grace; PG>=14; privileged attach detected not prevented.

brief.problem: Audit, cache, and evidence paths are tangled in storage.py with no tamper-evident audit store
brief.what_adds: Append-only AuditStore, clean module split, retention/redaction, checkpoint offload
brief.why: Compliance, maintainability, and storage cost control
brief.who_feels: Auditors, orchestrator maintainers, and storage operators

objective: EDP-20 slice 1: partition audit by RANGE(at) via a DDL-only migration plus a resumable Go swap tool (verified backup, batched idempotent copy, atomic rename under a short freeze), with per-leaf RLS/append-only and managed provisioning/retention (no lost events).
acceptance_criteria: 0014_audit_partitioning.up.sql is DDL-only, transactional and idempotent before the swap: it renames audit_id_seq to audit_legacy_id_seq, creates the shadow table, partitions, audit_id_seq, audit_partition_config, the primitives (attach/harden/assert/candidates/mark/drop/extract), audit_migration_state plus append-only state events, hold tables, audit_archive_manifest and grants, and is ensure-based (never drops partitions or lowers a live sequence). After a committed swap it refuses early with a clear error instead of recreating an empty shadow; down drops the substrate.

The shadow table is RANGE(at) monthly (UTC) with PK(id, at); partitions span legacy_min..current+3 plus one bounded audit_grace_YYYYMM for the month before legacy_min; ranges never overlap, no DEFAULT partition exists, and an out-of-range insert fails closed with 23514 and a stable message; audit_append_late(row, reason) is the audited operator path for corrected late evidence.

RLS is ENABLE+FORCE with tenant_isolation on the parent and every leaf; deny_mutation covers UPDATE/DELETE rows (never INSERT) on the parent and every leaf, and TRUNCATE is statement-level, so it is revoked from every role instead; app/tenant roles hold INSERT/SELECT on the parent ONLY (no grants on leaves), and a test proves one tenant cannot read another tenant's rows through any path.

Hardening is enforced by privilege: audit_attach_partition(month) is the only supported attach path (create + harden + attach in one transaction), ALTER/ATTACH is revoked from app and runtime roles, and audit_assert_hardened() DETECTS a privileged attach that skipped hardening, raising and emitting audit_attach_unhardened_total; a test proves the app/runtime roles cannot attach and that an unhardened leaf is detected.

The insert path fails closed with SQLSTATE 23514 + the stable 'no partition of relation' message when a month is missing; AuditStore.Append heals by calling audit_ensure_partitions(event month) under the AUDP advisory lock and retrying (bounded, 3 attempts), and provisioning is bounded to [now-24 months, now+horizon]. A BEFORE INSERT trigger cannot provision a partitioned table (PostgreSQL checks routing in the executor before row triggers - verified on PG16), so the trigger was removed rather than shipped inert.

Swap crash recovery is catalog-driven and idempotent: DetectState distinguishes not_prepared / prestage / swapped; if the rename committed, re-entry skips the swap and runs PostVerify (counts, per-tenant digest, sequence above max of audit and audit_legacy, assert_hardened) and records the committed state; the Postgres-16 integration suite exercises this resume path after a real swap.

Row count and a reproducible per-tenant SHA-256 over the ordered (id, tenant_id, action, at) rows are compared per batch and per tenant before the rename; a mismatch (or an id-reuse masked by ON CONFLICT) aborts the swap.

S4 sets lock_timeout=3s, takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE and THEN re-counts the delta inside the lock; a delta overflow OR a 55P03 lock timeout rolls back, releases the lock, backs off 1/2/4/8s and retries, bounded to 5 attempts then audit_swap_retry_exhausted and a non-zero exit; the achieved freeze time is emitted as audit_swap_freeze_seconds and compared with PF_AUDIT_FREEZE_BUDGET_SECONDS when set.

The swap is one atomic rename under a short ACCESS EXCLUSIVE window; no connection observes audit_partitioned, and AuditStore.Append retries then fails closed over the freeze; timing is asserted against the documented budget and emitted as audit_swap_freeze_seconds.

Retention primitives are SQL-only (audit_retention_candidates, audit_mark_archived, audit_drop_partition); go/cmd/pfaudit-retention is the single writer that exports the partition to ObjectStore with SSE-KMS, verifies a SHA-256 manifest, records it, drops the hot partition, and never touches current/future or grace; a dry-run lists candidates.

Row-level legal holds: audit_hold_extract(month) copies ONLY held rows into append-only audit_legal_hold_archive (FORCE tenant_isolation plus a pf_owner policy, tenant SELECT granted under RLS) with count/SHA-256 verification before export/drop; a hold placed AFTER archive triggers hold-reconcile (restore to scratch, extract, verify); recording a hold for a PURGED month is rejected and emits audit_hold_after_purge_total.

Purge and restore are Go-orchestrated and audited: pfaudit-retention removes archived objects only after purge_grace_days (default 90) and an explicit operator approval with dry-run; only that final purge is irreversible; restore re-imports a cold month into a scratch table whose leaves carry the standard RLS, and a round-trip test proves tenant isolation survives.

Operational tables are pf_owner-only with ALL revoked from app/tenant roles; audit_migration_state is a rebuildable projection of append-only audit_migration_state_events; both events tables deny UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE for every role via revokes plus a deny_mutation trigger; all retention/export/purge/hold/swap actions write audit events.

audit_partition_coverage() returns min/max month, grace bound and months_ahead; the EDP service startup check and the ops cron both emit audit_partition_months_ahead and audit_partition_low_coverage_total non-fatally and raise a stale-job alert; grace and audit_late_YYYYMM partitions (strictly below grace, non-overlapping) cannot satisfy coverage.

Advisory lock namespaces are separate and documented: AUDP (insert provisioning), AUSW (swap S4), AURE (retention/export/purge/restore); a test asserts the Go and SQL constants match and that retention does not block the insert slow path.

setval targets audit_id_seq explicitly: Phase 1 renames the legacy sequence to audit_legacy_id_seq and sets audit_id_seq to max(legacy id)+1; the shadow is not writable by app roles pre-swap; S4 sets it to greatest(legacy_max, shadow_max)+1 before commit; audit_partitioned.id defaults to audit_id_seq; the legacy sequence drops with audit_legacy; freshness, monotonicity and a fresh-install (empty audit, setval to 1) case are tested.

pfaudit-swap --down is gated: it refuses unless no month is archived/purged and no legal hold is active, renames audit_id_seq to audit_partitioned_id_seq and audit_legacy_id_seq back to audit_id_seq, asserts no id reuse against surviving rows, prints a dry-run and requires --force-with-reason (audited).

S1 backup is complete and lifespan-bound: pg_dump covers audit plus its sequence; the encrypted dump's readability is proven by a restore rehearsal (age -d | pg_restore -l) that asserts the table and sequence are present; close refuses until rollback_days has elapsed since the recorded swap unless --force-with-reason is given, and the dump is destroyed only after the recorded sign-off.

approach:
Two-phase design: the SQL migration is DDL-only; the destructive swap is a Go admin tool that runs OUTSIDE the migration transaction and persists its own state, so restart, backup and freeze are real and testable.

PHASE 1 - 0014_audit_partitioning.up.sql (DDL-only, transactional, idempotent; no row copy, no rename, no drop):
1. CREATE TABLE audit_partitioned (same columns as audit) PARTITION BY RANGE (at), PRIMARY KEY (id, at).
2. Create monthly UTC partitions audit_YYYYMM from legacy_min_month .. current+3, and exactly one bounded grace partition audit_grace_YYYYMM for the month BEFORE legacy_min_month (catches late writes older than the horizon). Ranges never overlap and there is NO DEFAULT partition. legacy_min is computed from audit (current-1 when empty).
3. CREATE SEQUENCE audit_id_seq; setval(max(audit.id)+1) (or 1 when empty) - no rows are copied.
4. Create audit_harden_partition(name): ENABLE+FORCE RLS + tenant_isolation policy + deny_mutation trigger for the parent and every leaf (RLS policies are not inherited). All SQL functions are SECURITY DEFINER with a pinned search_path (pg_catalog, public) and owned by pf_owner; EXECUTE is revoked from app/tenant roles.
5. Create audit_ensure_partitions(months_ahead) idempotent under pg_advisory_xact_lock with 42P07 retry; every created partition is hardened.
6. BEFORE INSERT trigger on audit_partitioned: FAST PATH reads the provisioned horizon and returns without any lock when the month is covered; only a missing month takes the advisory lock, creates+hardens the partition, retries on 42P07. The trigger is the last line of defence.
7. audit_partition_coverage() returns min month, max month, grace bound and months_ahead (the lead-time check cannot be satisfied by the grace partition alone).
8. audit_legal_hold_events is append-only (action HOLD|RELEASE, tenant_id, from_at, to_at, reason, at); active holds are computed from events, so releasing a hold never UPDATEs a row. audit_apply_retention(keep_months, dry_run) clamps keep_months >= 1, skips any partition overlapped by an active hold and reports held/skipped count + oldest held partition.
9. Recreate the enumerated dependent views explicitly (no CASCADE); the pairing test asserts both files and the structural assertions.

PHASE 2 - Go admin tool go/cmd/pfaudit-swap (outside migrate.LoadDir; state persisted BETWEEN transactions):
S0 preflight: PG >= 14, pinned pg_dump/restore versions in the runbook, partition coverage.
S1 backup: pg_dump -t audit, restore into a scratch schema, record dump checksum + restore row count in audit_migration_state (state=DONE only after the restore proves the data).
S2 pre-stage copy in batches (e.g. 10k) ordered by id: INSERT INTO audit_partitioned ... ON CONFLICT (id, at) DO NOTHING; persist last_id + copied count in a separate transaction after EACH batch, so a crash resumes from last_id without duplicates or partial-load corruption.
S3 verify: row count, max(id) and a per-tenant count checksum between audit and audit_partitioned; mismatch aborts before any rename.
S4 short swap: LOCK audit IN ACCESS EXCLUSIVE (bounded write-freeze), drain the delta (id > last_id), re-verify, then in ONE transaction rename audit -> audit_legacy and audit_partitioned -> audit, setval(max(id)+1), commit. The freeze covers only the delta rename, not the full copy; AuditStore.Append retries with backoff and fails closed if the window is exceeded. Measured freeze budget is recorded.
S5 post-swap: verify counts/checksums on the live audit, confirm views resolve, then keep audit_legacy until the operator signs off (dropped by a separate audited step, never inside 0014).

Deployments with an empty audit take the same path (copy is a no-op) so the code path is always exercised.

DOWN - go/cmd/pfaudit-swap --down: rebuild a non-partitioned audit_rebuilt from the surviving partitions with row-count/ordering verification under the same pf_owner-only, bounded-freeze rules, atomically rename back, restore sequence/triggers/RLS/grants; drop leaves and the parent. Data already dropped by retention is unrecoverable and documented.

Contract/API: no new route. needs_api=false because AuditStore.Append and the /audit admin op keep their signatures and tenant scoping; the only change is the physical table. PK(id, at) keeps lookup-by-id unique (ids are sequence-generated); a test enumerates FKs/constraints/indexes/callers and proves no breakage. Rows are never updated or deleted by the swap.

FREEZE/SEQUENCE/STATE HARDENING (Gate 1.5 re-review):
- Delta bound is ENFORCED, not measured: before taking ACCESS EXCLUSIVE, S4 counts rows with id > last_id; if the delta exceeds audit.partition.swap_max_delta_rows (default 5000) or the estimated drain exceeds 60s, abort, run another pre-stage batch, and retry. The lock is only taken when the delta is provably small.
- Sequence handoff is explicit: Phase 1 creates audit_new_id_seq owned by pf_owner and sets it to max(legacy audit.id)+1; legacy keeps its own BIGSERIAL sequence until it is renamed to audit_legacy. Before the swap commit, S4 sets audit_new_id_seq to greatest(legacy_max_id, partitioned_max_id)+1, and audit_partitioned.id DEFAULT nextval('audit_new_id_seq') is the ONLY id source after the rename. The legacy sequence is dropped with audit_legacy.
- Out-of-range write fail-closed: with no DEFAULT partition, a row whose at falls outside the monthly+grace ranges fails with a clear SQLSTATE 23514 message and increments audit_insert_out_of_range_total. This is an accepted, documented risk (clock skew/backdated events); the grace partition is the only legitimate older window and the runbook states the first action.
- audit_migration_state (key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value JSONB, updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ) is created in Phase 1, owned by pf_owner, with DML/EXECUTE revoked from pf_app/pf_runtime/tenant roles; changes are recorded in an append-only audit_migration_state_events table (actor, from_state, to_state, at) and are audited. Small, no retention.
- Coverage signal is defined and non-fatal: audit_partition_months_ahead gauge + audit_partition_low_coverage_total counter; startup logs+emits a non-fatal alert event (never crashes the deploy); the scheduled job emits the same and pages at < 2 months. The insert trigger remains the last line of defence.
- Advisory lock key is a pinned constant (0x41554449, 'AUDI'), documented in the ADR.
- audit_harden_partition is re-runnable and versioned: audit_partition_policy_version records the applied version, and an upgrade re-runs harden on every leaf when the version changes.
- S3 checksum is reproducible: per-tenant md5 over the ordered (id, tenant_id, action, at) rows, compared per tenant AND per batch, so a swallowed ON CONFLICT cannot hide an id-reuse defect.
- Grace retention: audit_grace_YYYYMM is dropped/recreated only by the swap tooling, never by audit_apply_retention; if legacy_min never moves it stays bounded to one month (stated in the runbook).
- Down/retention docs are pinned: EDP-17-SCHEMA section 'Retention irreversibility' and the ADR addendum.
- Config constants (single source): audit.partition_horizon_months=3, audit.partition_lead_months=2, audit.swap_batch_rows=10000, audit.swap_max_delta_rows=5000 (recorded in the runbook with the measured freeze).
- Tests use a strict grace pattern (audit_grace_\d{6}) so LIKE 'audit_%' globs do not conflate grace with monthly partitions.

ENTERPRISE RETENTION + ROW-LEVEL HOLDS (folded into this slice):
- Row-level legal holds: a pre-drop step extracts ONLY rows under an active hold into audit_legal_hold_archive (append-only, FORCE tenant_isolation RLS, per-row hold_id, reason, held_at, source_partition). Retention REFUSES to export/drop a partition until held-row extraction is verified (count+checksum), so a hold never pins a whole partition and never loses a held row.
- Two-stage retention: (A) HOT->COLD: for a month fully older than keep_months, export the partition to the existing ObjectStore adapter (go/objstore, s3store/gcsstore) as immutable objects plus a SHA-256 manifest; request WORM/Object-Lock retention where the adapter reports support, else immutable keys + a hash-chained ledger row. Record audit_archive_manifest (row_count, checksum, object keys, archived_at), verify it, THEN drop the hot partition. (B) COLD->PURGE: audit_purge_archive deletes archived objects only after purge_grace_days (default 90) AND an explicit audited operator approval, dry-run first. Only this final purge is irreversible.
- audit_restore_archive(month) re-imports a cold month into a scratch partitioned table for legal/audit requests; a restore drill is in the runbook.
- A hold on an archived month blocks the PURGE (not the export); releases are append-only audit_legal_hold_events, never UPDATEs.
- Backups: backup retention >= legal retention (PITR window pinned in config/runbook) and a quarterly restore drill are required; the swap backup is not the retention safety net.
- Privileges: export/purge/restore functions are pf_owner-only (EXECUTE revoked from app/tenant); every export/purge/hold action writes an audit event.

GATE 1.5 ROUND-3 RESOLUTIONS (ownership + enforced invariants):
- Primitives vs orchestration (CL-001 single writer): SQL owns ONLY set-based primitives - audit_retention_candidates(), audit_mark_archived(month, manifest jsonb), audit_drop_partition(month), audit_hold_extract(month), audit_purge_candidates(), audit_mark_purged(month). Object-storage I/O is Go-owned in go/cmd/pfaudit-retention (export, verify, purge objects, restore). No SQL function calls S3/GCS.
- Out-of-range write: the trigger RAISEs 23514 with a stable message/hint (no counter UPDATE in the same transaction, which would roll back). AuditStore.Append maps that SQLSTATE to the Go Prometheus counter audit_insert_out_of_range_total and logs a structured event; an admin path audit_append_late(row, reason) (SECURITY DEFINER, pf_owner-only, audited) re-inserts late evidence after correction.
- Backup handling: pg_dump is piped through age (encrypted) straight into the ObjectStore under audit-backup/<run>/ with server-side encryption, accessible only to pf_owner/ops; manifest hash recorded; the dump is destroyed after the verified swap (documented in the runbook). No plaintext cross-tenant dump on disk.
- Freeze bound is enforced under the lock: S4 sets lock_timeout=3s, takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE, THEN re-counts rows with id > last_id; if count > swap_max_delta_rows it rolls back (releasing the lock), runs another pre-stage batch and retries. The count outside the lock is only a pre-check.
- Advisory lock namespaces are separate: insert-path provisioning uses 0x41554450 ('AUDP'), swap S4 uses 0x41555357 ('AUSW'), retention/export/purge/restore uses 0x41555245 ('AURE'). Retention therefore never blocks a missing-month insert. All documented in the ADR.
- Hardening is ENFORCED, not procedural: an event trigger on ddl_command_end for 'ATTACH PARTITION' verifies and applies audit_harden_partition on the new leaf (and RAISEs if it cannot), so a direct ATTACH cannot create an unprotected leaf. ATTACH is also revoked from app/tenant roles.
- Privilege boundary reconciled: app/tenant roles hold INSERT/SELECT on the PARENT ONLY; leaves grant NOTHING to app/tenant roles (access flows through the parent, where RLS applies). audit_harden_partition therefore applies RLS+policy+deny_mutation but NO app grants on the leaf.
- Operational tables are NOT tenant-RLS: audit_migration_state, audit_archive_manifest, audit_legal_hold_events, audit_legal_hold_archive_meta are owned by pf_owner with ALL revoked from app/tenant roles and no blanket policy. audit_legal_hold_archive is tenant-scoped WITH tenant_isolation FORCE plus an explicit pf_owner policy (USING true) so SECURITY DEFINER functions work without leaking to tenants.
- pfaudit-retention is the single writer for retention/export/purge/restore (Go); it calls the SQL primitives only. audit_apply_retention is replaced by these primitives (no overlapping duties).
- --down is gated: it refuses unless (a) no month has been archived or purged (manifest empty) and (b) no active legal hold exists; it prints a dry-run and requires --force-with-reason, which is audited. Down never silently reconstructs a legally incomplete table.
- Retention/export/coverage job ownership is named: go/cmd/pfaudit-retention run by the ops cron (documented schedule) AND invoked at EDP service startup for the coverage check; both emit the same audit_partition_months_ahead gauge + low-coverage counter, and a missing heartbeat raises a stale-job alert event.
- Fast-path horizon is a single-row audit_partition_config table (horizon_months, lead_months, batch_rows, max_delta_rows) read by prepared statement/session cache and updated only by pf_owner; it is not a per-insert catalog scan and changes are seen on next plan/parse.
- The shadow table is not writable by app/tenant roles before the swap; only the swap tool (pf_owner) writes audit_partitioned, so its id DEFAULT cannot be consumed pre-S4; S4 sets audit_new_id_seq = greatest(legacy_max, shadow_max)+1 in the swap transaction.
- Cold archive: keys are audit/cold/<YYYYMM>/part-000.parquet with SSE-KMS at rest, bucket policy restricted to the retention role, no per-tenant splitting (all tenants in one object); restore re-imports into a scratch partitioned table whose leaves get the standard RLS, so tenant isolation is preserved after re-import.
- Integrity primitive is SHA-256 everywhere (copy verify, batch verify, archive manifest, hash chain); per-tenant compare is (count, sha256 over ordered rows). md5 is dropped.
- Metrics: audit_partition_months_ahead (gauge), audit_partition_low_coverage_total, audit_insert_out_of_range_total, audit_provision_seconds (histogram), audit_swap_freeze_seconds, audit_copy_batch_total{resumed}, audit_export_total{outcome}, audit_drop_total, audit_purge_total, audit_hold_extract_total, audit_late_insert_total.

GATE 1.5 ROUND-4 RESOLUTIONS (privilege-safe enforcement, backup lifetime, late/hold gaps):
- NO event trigger (it needs superuser and is database-wide). Hardening is enforced by privilege: the ONLY supported path is audit_attach_partition(month) (SECURITY DEFINER) which creates, hardens and attaches in one transaction; ALTER on the partitioned table (and ATTACH) is revoked from app/tenant roles and from the runtime role. audit_assert_hardened() re-checks every leaf (RLS enabled+forced, policy present, deny_mutation present) and is called by the provisioner, the coverage job and the test suite; a failure RAISEs and blocks the swap. Residual: a superuser/pf_owner manual ATTACH is out of the application trust boundary and is detected by the assert + audit event.
- Backup lifetime matches the rollback contract: the age-encrypted pg_dump stays in the ObjectStore for rollback_window_days (default 14, configurable) and is destroyed ONLY after a recorded sign-off in audit_migration_state (swap_closed), never immediately after the swap. Rollback therefore has a true restore until sign-off; pfaudit-swap --down is a separate, gated path.
- Hold-after-archive is covered: when a hold is placed on an already-archived month, pfaudit-retention performs hold-reconcile - restore the month into a scratch table, extract the held rows into audit_legal_hold_archive with count+SHA-256 verification, record hold_extracted, then allow the purge only after that. A hold therefore never depends on the cold object staying readable.
- Late evidence older than grace: audit_append_late(row, reason) provisions a bounded ad-hoc audit_late_YYYYMM partition (lookback <= 24 months), inserts, records an audit event and is excluded from coverage; retention archives late partitions like normal ones. pf_owner-only and audited.
- The insert fast path reads audit_partition_config directly with a prepared statement (single-row PK lookup, no application-side cache and no TTL), so a config UPDATE is visible immediately and PostgreSQL handles plan invalidation; a test asserts a changed horizon takes effect on the next insert.
- Trigger contract is explicit: the provisioning trigger is BEFORE INSERT and runs first (name audit_provision_trg); deny_mutation is a separate trigger for UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE only (never INSERT); a pg_trigger ordering test asserts both fire in the required order.
- Swap retries are bounded: at most 5 attempts with 1/2/4/8/16s backoff, then exit non-zero with audit_swap_retry_exhausted and an alert; an operator re-runs after investigating. No unbounded livelock.
- Language rule: the SQL objects are single-purpose set-based DDL/DML primitives (attach+harden, candidates, mark, drop, extract, assert) with no workflow, retries, I/O or state machine; ALL orchestration and object-storage I/O is Go (pfaudit-swap, pfaudit-retention). This split is recorded in the ADR so CL-001 (Go single writer) and the SQL primitives do not conflict.
- audit_migration_state is a PROJECTION: the append-only audit_migration_state_events is the source of truth and state is rebuildable from it (a rebuild function is tested); the key-value table is a cache for fast gating, never authoritative alone.
- Config single source: audit_partition_config is authoritative; Go reads it at startup and refuses to start if its compiled constants (advisory keys, batch/delta defaults) disagree with the row; a test asserts SQL and Go lock keys match.
- Down path recreates an equivalent sequence: pfaudit-swap --down creates audit_id_seq_new, sets it above max(surviving id) and asserts no id reuse before attaching the default; this is an AC, not just prose.
- KMS/object layout: SSE-KMS with a dedicated key, bucket policy limited to the retention role and the audit/cold/<YYYYMM>/ prefix; per-tenant splitting is deferred by decision (documented) because tenant isolation is restored by RLS on re-import.
- Metrics add: audit_swap_retry_total, audit_swap_retry_exhausted_total, audit_hold_extract_failed_total, audit_attach_unhardened_total (assert failures).
- Grace partition is a fixed historical artifact created once at swap and never moved by retention; it retires only via an explicit archived-and-purged decision, stated in the runbook.

GATE 1.5 ROUND-5 RESOLUTIONS (canonical names + crash/hold/privilege invariants):
- CANONICAL SEQUENCE NAMES (one name per object): Phase 1 renames the legacy sequence audit_id_seq -> audit_legacy_id_seq, then CREATEs audit_id_seq for the shadow and setvals it to max(legacy id)+1. audit_partitioned.id DEFAULT nextval('audit_id_seq'). The swap renames only the TABLES (audit -> audit_legacy, audit_partitioned -> audit); the sequences are already correctly named. --down renames audit_id_seq -> audit_partitioned_id_seq and audit_legacy_id_seq -> audit_id_seq. No other name is used anywhere.
- Attach AC restated honestly: attach/create is DENIED to app/runtime roles (privilege-enforced); audit_assert_hardened() DETECTS any privileged (pf_owner/superuser) attach that skipped hardening and raises + emits audit_attach_unhardened_total. We do not claim a privileged attach is impossible.
- Crash resume beyond S2 is defined by a catalog-driven state machine: on start, pfaudit-swap inspects pg_class/pg_sequence state. If audit_partitioned exists and audit is the live table -> resume copy/verify. If audit_legacy exists and audit is partitioned -> the rename committed: skip to post-swap verify (sequence >= max, counts, assert_hardened), then mark swap_committed. Every step is idempotent and a failure-injection test kills the process after the rename and proves re-entry completes.
- Lock-timeout (55P03) is handled explicitly: it is treated like a delta overflow - rollback, backoff (1/2/4/8/16s), retry up to 5 attempts, then exit with audit_swap_retry_exhausted.
- S1 backup completeness is enumerated and verified: pg_dump -t audit includes the table, its DEFAULT, the sequence, triggers and grants; dependent views are dumped explicitly. Restore verification checks row count, sequence name and next value, DEFAULT presence, trigger count and grant set - not row count alone.
- Hold-after-PURGE is closed: recording a hold for a purged month is REJECTED at insert time with a stable error and emits audit_hold_after_purge_total (spoliation alert); the residual (evidence already destroyed before the hold existed) is documented in the ADR.
- audit_legal_hold_archive grants are explicit: pf_owner full; tenant roles SELECT via tenant_isolation RLS (held rows are tenant data and must stay readable after the partition drops); app writes are denied. The cross-tenant test covers this table too.
- TRUNCATE is privilege-enforced, not trigger-only: TRUNCATE is REVOKED from app/tenant/runtime roles on the parent and leaves, and deny_mutation also covers TRUNCATE as defence in depth.
- audit_migration_state_events and audit_legal_hold_events are append-only by BOTH mechanisms: no UPDATE/DELETE grants to any non-owner role and a deny_mutation trigger (UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE) even for pf_owner.
- 0014 re-run is ensure-based: it never drops/recreates existing partitions, never re-setvals a live audit_id_seq below its last value (uses GREATEST(current, max+1)), and is covered by a second-apply test.
- audit_late_YYYYMM invariant: strictly below the grace month, non-overlapping with monthly/grace ranges; the test glob uses audit_late_\d{6} explicitly.
- Purge approval records actor, timestamp and reason in audit_archive_manifest (not just a CLI flag).
- Config relationship pinned in one block: backup_retention_days >= legal_retention_days >= keep_months*31 + purge_grace_days; validated at startup.

Postgres-16 integration suite (pfaudit): 0014 second-apply idempotency, copy/verify/swap, crash-resume PostVerify, divergence detection, per-tenant RLS isolation, leaf INSERT denial, unhardened-leaf detection, active-hold and current-month drop refusal, hold extract+verify, export->manifest->drop->purge, restore-after-purge refusal
PG16 integration suite: reconcile-after-archive round trip (restore -> extract -> digest verify -> scratch drop) and coverage/stale probe emit the AC metrics.
Privilege-boundary test: pf_app denied audit_mark_archived/approve_purge/drop_partition and raw ATTACH (permission denied).
Down copy-back aborts if any post-swap row is still missing from the flat table; AURE is held by restore/reconcile too.
edpsvc startup probe + /admin/audit-coverage read coverage via the store port (no pgx import); ops cron sample in ops/cron.
risks: Out-of-range audit write fails closed: surfaced via the Go metric and the audited audit_append_late path (bounded ad-hoc month).
Delta may arrive between pre-check and lock: mitigated by re-counting under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE with lock_timeout and bounded retries.
Superuser manual ATTACH outside the app boundary: detected by audit_assert_hardened and audited; app/runtime roles cannot attach.
Retention could block insert provisioning: mitigated by separate advisory-lock namespaces plus a constant-match test.
Post-swap defect after backup destruction: prevented by keeping the encrypted dump until the recorded swap_closed sign-off.
Hold placed after archive: covered by hold-reconcile (restore, extract, verify) before purge.
Late evidence older than grace: covered by bounded audit_late_YYYYMM partitions via audit_append_late.
Cross-tenant backup/cold objects: age/SSE-KMS encryption, pf_owner/ops-only access, hash manifest, per-tenant split deferred by documented decision.
Down after retention: gated by archive/hold checks, sequence recreation and audited --force-with-reason.
SQL vs Go ownership tension: SQL is limited to single-purpose primitives; all orchestration and I/O is Go (recorded in the ADR).
A privileged (pf_owner/superuser) attach outside the app boundary: detected by audit_assert_hardened and audited; not preventable by privilege alone.
Evidence destroyed before a hold is recorded (post-purge): rejected at hold insert with a spoliation alert; residual documented in the ADR.
Crash after the rename: handled by the catalog-driven resume state machine and a kill-after-rename test.
rollback: go/cmd/pfaudit-swap --down rebuilds non-partitioned audit from surviving partitions with verification and restores sequence/triggers/RLS/grants; the verified pg_dump backup restores the pre-swap state. Retention-dropped data is unrecoverable (documented).
